term: when pairs suffice: the Helly number of a rule class

Byte verification also needs a medium that preserves bytes, with no conversion in either direction (S0137 L209) (a store normalising line endings on checkout breaks the hash without touching meaning; S0136 L297).

term: checkable is not checked
meaning: A re-runnable (reproducible) check lets a reader verify without trusting the producer, but until another party re-runs it the result rests on the producer's report (L1a). Re-runnability holds only for the named input cut. A completeness check against a list (here the commission's) cannot see the list's omissions. A recorded re-run by a party independent in authorship moves a mechanical result from checkable to checked (one sufficient route; an independent re-derivation is another, §8.19 C10); for judgements (e.g. conformity) independence of stake is a further condition.

term: a commitment detects loss only of what it committed to (a corollary of K1)
meaning: A corollary of §9.15 K1 ("relative to a commitment kept outside"): an external anchor detects the loss of the entries it committed to, at its own cut; an uncited tail or a whole record added after it and then lost is not detected by comparison with it (a numbered successor still reveals a loss, K1 I-07). The anchor must be taken again at the operation it protects. A count is not a commitment; a hash of the entries shows that the set differs, only a list shows what differs. Over a multi-step operation, the anchor must guard the destructive step: a claim bounded to the observed inputs is honest and can be self-satisfying, since what was not observed is in neither input (S0137 RC-4). Guarding the destructive step is necessary, not sufficient: an interval between the final check and the act stays irreducible without serialisation (S0138 L116). The operand condition is split off as CON-0259.

term: two lifecycles, two locations
meaning: Evidence is written once and never revised; execution state is rebuilt on demand; so what has the record's lifecycle lives where that lifecycle is kept, and the recomputable may live anywhere. A store holding both cannot give either its own durability (the estate's inversion, CON-0233). In the book: G3 (every change an entry) and CE* computing standing from the record; S0131 adds the placement consequence. A producer's criterion, not a decision. Premise: one durability policy per store; with per-path policies inside one store, "cannot give either its own durability" does not follow (A-16).

term: acknowledged is not recorded
meaning: A writer whose read-modify-write is not serialised can acknowledge an append (exit 0, a seq) that a concurrent write then overwrites; the surviving sequence stays dense. An acknowledgement is evidence that the write happened, not that it survived. L9 ("record before use") therefore needs K6 (serialised steps): an acceptance that does not follow the serialised commit of a state containing the entry is not an acceptance in L9's sense. Incomplete without durability: an acknowledged write can also be lost by a crash (no fsync), so L9 needs K6's serialisation (law 12, atomic change) and K1's durability. Applying K6 to the estate's writer (outside D) is by analogy.

term: for readers outside the resolver, the status must be in the artifact
meaning: A status held elsewhere (a declaration, registry or resolver) reaches only readers who consult it; readers outside it choose by discoverability, which can run against authority (the staging copy, least authoritative, is the most discoverable). For such readers a copy's status must be marked in the artifact itself, or the copy made unreachable. In D each entry carries its own status; CON-0246 concerns which store a copy is. For byte-verified evidence an in-file marker is impossible (it breaks the hash) and an out-of-band marker does not reach the reader who opens only the record, so only unreachability, or a status carried in the path by which the record is reached (e.g. the store's name, changing no byte), reaches that reader; otherwise the status is advisory to it (S0137 L182–186). An out-of-band marker is a second record with its own lifecycle and becomes false unless retracted when the status changes (S0138 RD-7).

term: the operator's own writes must be named in advance
meaning: When the operation guarded by an anchor writes its own evidence into the record it guards, "nothing was written" is false by design; a violation can be told from the operator's bookkeeping only if the expected writes are named in advance. The checkable claim becomes "nothing was written except the named entries"; since expected entries are known before the operation only by kind and actor, the expected list is a predicate (kinds, lane, window), not a set of identities. The predicate must bind an authenticated actor (§9.15 L10); with self-declared lanes, a writer declaring the migration lane passes as expected, so only honest violators are detected (window C26, S0140).

meaning: A status held outside the artifact (declaration, registry, resolver, out-of-band marker) reaches only readers who consult it; readers outside the resolver choose by discoverability, which can run against authority. Byte-verified evidence cannot carry an in-file status, so for a reader who opens only the record, only keeping non-authoritative copies out of reach binds; otherwise the status is advisory to that reader. An out-of-band marker is a second record with its own lifecycle and becomes false unless retracted.

term: nothing written except the declared
meaning: When the operation guarded by an anchor writes its own evidence into the record it guards, the checkable claim is "nothing written except the declared". It is detected by a non-trivial declaration (one that excludes something) plus either authenticated actors (L10) or the operator's own identity log of its writes, at entry granularity (a per-file check masks writes to the operator's own file). Losses among the declared writes remain undetectable. The declaration must exclude what a violator could write, and the operator's identity log is the operator's testimony, which itself needs an anchor (A-16).

term: an undisposed quarantine is a hold
meaning: An item held undecided (quarantined, never reconciled, never promoted) blocks every act that needs it decided, and forbids every act that would destroy it; so it is a hold, released only by a disposition act of the competent authority. Retaining the whole store preserves the bytes; the hold is needed to block completion and moves. It must be an explicit hold state independent of where the item sits, with a gate on moves; a hold inferred from a comparison can be released silently by moving the item. D records every removal (G3) but has no state that forbids one.

meaning: A record cannot contain a complete, current statement of a state that includes the statement itself (a prefix statement, e.g. a hash of earlier entries, is possible). Where every write must be evidenced by an append in the same store, closing that store has no fixed point; the closing record must lie in another record and order the closed store's writes by naming its head (CON-0251).

term: rediscovering known defects shows reach, not detection
meaning: A checker validated by rediscovering defects already found and named, written after them and against the same artifacts, shows that each check reaches those defects; it does not show detection of unknown ones. Validation has at least three axes (exhaustiveness not shown): novelty of the instance (known defect, fresh instance of a known class, new class), independence of the planter (checker author, rules author, independent), and blinding (key sealed or not). S0143 is known instances (S3 not even that, fixture-fed); S0144 is fresh instances, rules-author planter, unsealed. A structural checker detects a missing act only if the act is referenced somewhere; acts referenced nowhere need review. A quiet row is evidence only within the implemented scope.

term: a reference derived from the checked state cannot fail
meaning: The reference a gate compares against must be closed before the act it validates, must cover every change the survivor is meant to carry (too early a reference fails in the normal case), and must be derived from the other side (not from the state the act produced); a reference derived after the act from its own result compares a thing with itself. Rival: a sequencing slip a careful reader avoids. Falsifier: a check whose reference comes only from the checked object yet detects a defect (impossible unless the derivation reads an independent input, which meets the third condition).

term: a reference computed from the survivor alone cannot detect its divergence
meaning: To detect that a survivor (copy, result) differs from its intended state, the reference must be (i) exactly the intended state and (ii) computed from an input independent of the survivor. A reference that is a function of the survivor alone can catch internal inconsistency but not that divergence. The order in which the reference is closed is an executability matter (data dependency), not a condition. Rival: dependency inversion; the test-oracle problem (Ext). Falsifier: a check whose reference is a function of the survivor alone yet detects divergence from the source. Scope: replacement gates; one lineage (S0142, S0146); hypothesis beyond.

term: a reference must carry information the act cannot rewrite
meaning: To detect that a survivor differs from its intended state, the reference must carry information that originates independently of the checked content and that the act being checked cannot rewrite; where the reference is stored does not matter. A reference whose information comes only from the checked content can catch internal inconsistency, not divergence. Prior work: the test-oracle problem (Ext: Barr et al. 2015, not opened), established, adapted to replacement gates. Rival: dependency inversion. term: the designated record (K2 restated)
meaning: The record (the entries the kernel's steps accepted) is distinct from its carrier (the store holding it); which store carries it is set by a designation, an act, not by its entries (R1). Old K2 follows within one designation; reading 1 of old K2 (readers agree with one another) does not imply K2-w/K2-r (M2). K2-w, K2-r and K1 independent. The restatement makes the referent explicit (a re-axiomatisation, not a derivation).

term: membership by acceptance; classification across a carrier change
meaning: An entry is a member of a record iff a kernel step accepted it into the record (appended it to the carrier designated at that time); carried-across copies are the same members. Without a trusted order shared with the designation, entry content cannot place an entry on one side of a carrier change (two-history proof); with trusted shared recording time it can (epoch). A designation change recorded with an exact closing list of the old carrier (premise: no member lost before it) gives a conservative classification: in the list, member; outside, classed foreign (withheld, not promoted); writes between the list and the switch misclassified, irreducible without serialisation. Sealing the old carrier is another route. Decided 2026-10-25: each change of carrier is a designation entry in D citing the last entry under the old carrier; membership across the change is then decided from the record (the cited prefix), order by citation, not recording time; with serialised kernel steps (K6) no member falls between the cited entry and the designation (model v16, check 28).

term: the carrier-change gate: survivor and casualty against an outside list
meaning: Before retiring the old carrier of a record (an architecture act; D has no carriers), a check that the survivor holds an exact outside list and that the casualty holds nothing outside it (anything outside is classed foreign and blocks) detects every loss of a member the casualty held at the check; a survivor-only gate misses members accepted after the list was taken; a survivor-derived list detects nothing; a member lost from the casualty after an outside list covered it is detected only through that list; members lost before any read are out of reach; writes between check and act need serialisation. Coverage (CON-0243), independence as its means (CON-0257) and the operand, survivor not only casualty (CON-0259), are aspects of one gate, not three independent conditions. Kernel part: K1's refutation by an outside commitment that covers the entries and is not derived from the carrier.
